_comment: Per-document invariant exemptions. An invariant listed here still RUNS, and its
failures are still counted and printed -- they just do not fail the build for the
one document named in `applies_to`. Everything else on the lane still gates.
`applies_to` is a substring of metadata.filename, the same scoping rule cases use.
`invariant` must name an entry in the lane's ALL_INVARIANTS (a test asserts this,
so a typo is a failure rather than a silently ineffective exemption).
Every entry below was traced to its source PDF before being written. The bar for
adding one is that the invariant is RIGHT and the document is genuinely outside
what the pipeline can read today -- never that a check is inconvenient. If an
exemption's invariant starts passing, the suite says so and the entry is deleted.

exemptions.reason: Compilation, not a single instrument. The 563-page document's TOC is an index of 44 separately-notified rule sets ('17. Duty and Tax Remission (DTRE) for Export S.R.O.185(I)/2020'), each of which restarts its own rule numbering, so codes cannot ascend document-wide. The tree has no level above chapter for 'instrument' and six walkers hardcode chapter/part/division/section as the child keys. Needs the ingest feature in tasks.md Phase 6 option (a).

The source PDF's text layer emits the run as ONE 75-character token with no space glyphs inside it, so there is no positional information to split on. Recovering the spaces needs dictionary or language-model word splitting, which is non-deterministic and excluded by the README's 'no LLM/vision in the conversion path'.
Same cause as Customs Rules above: a single jammed token in the source PDF's text layer, no space glyphs to split on.
Same cause: jammed tokens in the source PDF's text layer, e.g. 'whetherthemonthlyreturnsfurnishedbytheregisteredpersoncorrectlyreflect' arrives from pdfplumber as one token.

The parser refuses this merge DELIBERATELY. Footnote 54.104 prints 'dated 21 st June, 2006'; pagemodel's discriminators for a raised suffix are a size drop and the absence of a space glyph, and this token is equal size (8.04pt), dtop 0.00, with a real space -- indistinguishable from a genuine '21 st' typo in the source. Merging it would merge real typos too. The invariant does not know the parser made that choice.
Same deliberate parser refusal as the 2005 edition above: an equal-size, space-separated ordinal suffix that cannot be told apart from a source typo.

Same compilation as the section_codes_ordered entry above, measured on the same 44 S.R.O. rule-sets. The tree has no level above chapter, so the 563-page binder's INDEX rows become the section leaves: 'Passenger's Baggage (Import)Rules. 570(I)/98 dt.12.06.1998', 'Frustrated Cargo Export Rules 3(I)/70, dt 2.1.1970 86-89'. A leaf built from an index row has no body to carry, and 44 of the lane's 111 hits are exactly those rows. The invariant is right and the pipeline cannot express the document; the fix is the 'instrument' tree level in wip/tasks.md Phase 5, whose completion is the deletion of this entry.

The mirror of the section_carries_its_body entry above, on the same 44 index rows and the same evidence. That invariant names the starved leaf; this one names the leaf whose body the index row landed in, and it fires 3 times here for exactly the reason the other fires 44: an index row is not a rule. Measured: rule 3's body holds '7. Jurisdiction _____________________' (an index row with its leaders), rule 5's holds '6 Annexure-E.2 Legal Compliance YES YES YES' (an annexure table row) and rule 1's holds '15.06.2002.' (an S.R.O. date read as rule 15). All three victims are index-row leaves already covered above. Exempted here rather than left red because the pair must agree: the pipeline cannot express this document either way. Same fix, same deletion condition -- the 'instrument' tree level in wip/tasks.md Phase 5.

Compilation in miniature. PDF page 75 starts a second instrument inside the body -- 'ELECTRONIC FILING OF FEDERAL EXCISE RETURN RULES, 2005' with its own CONTENTS page -- and that contents page's rows are parsed as this document's rules 1-4, so they carry leader dots where their text should be: 'Short title, application and commencement___________________', 'Filing of Electronic Federal Excise Return__________________'. A leaf built from a contents row has no body to carry. Same missing 'instrument' tree level as Customs Rules, 2001 above; the fix is wip/tasks.md Phase 5, whose completion is the deletion of this entry. (This document's section_codes_ordered exemption, which recorded the same page-75 evidence, was deleted in the same change -- the suite reported it as no longer failing.)

The mirror of the section_carries_its_body entry above, on the same page-75 evidence. Rule 1's body holds '2. Definitions.--1n these Rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the' -- the real opening of the SECOND instrument, whose contents rows were parsed as this document's rules 1-4. The victim is one of those four contents-row leaves, so the two invariants are reporting the two halves of one defect and only one of them was written down. Same fix, same deletion condition -- the 'instrument' tree level in wip/tasks.md Phase 5.
